section.content: Example embodiments of the present disclosure relate to solutions for improving Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Learning (ML) localization. In one aspect, a terminal device sends a request to a network device for a neural network module cascaded after a pre-training model. The terminal device receives from the network device a sequence of trained neural network modules concatenated after the pre-training model and a set of input signals from a set of Transmission Reception Points (TRPs) to be input to the terminal device. The terminal device performs AI/ML localization by using the input signal sets from the TRP sets in the above order based on trained neural network modules cascaded after the pre-training model. In this way, a trade-off between model performance, model complexity, and computational complexity may be achieved.

本公开的示例实施例涉及用于改进人工智能（AI）或机器学习（ML）定位的解决方案。在一个方面，一种终端设备向网络设备发送针对在预训练模型之后级联的神经网络模块的请求。终端设备从网络设备接收在预训练模型之后级联的经训练的神经网络模块和要输入到终端设备的来自传输接收点（TRP）集的输入信号集的顺序。终端设备基于在预训练模型之后级联的经训练的神经网络模块，通过按上述顺序使用来自TRP集的输入信号集来执行AI/ML定位。以这种方式，可以实现模型性能、模型复杂度和计算复杂度之间的权衡。

Improved artificial intelligence or machine learning positioningTechnical Field

Various example embodiments relate to the field of communications, and in particular, to devices, methods, apparatuses, and computer-readable storage media for improving Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Learning (ML) positioning.

Background

From a standardization perspective, 3GPP release 18 has approved research to enhance the benefits of the air interface through recent advances in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Learning (ML), and AI/ML positioning accuracy enhancement is considered one of the three most representative use cases, e.g., positioning accuracy enhancement for different scenarios, including scenarios with severe NLOS conditions. AI/ML localization (e.g., direct AI/ML localization) is considered an important aspect of further research. Thus, there is a need for improved AI/ML localization.

Disclosure of Invention

In general, example embodiments of the present disclosure provide a solution to improve AI/ML localization, such as direct AI/ML localization.

In a first aspect, a terminal device is provided. The terminal device may include at least one processor and at least one memory storing instructions that, when executed by the at least one processor, cause the terminal device to at least transmit a request to a network device for a neural network module cascaded after a pre-training model, receive from the network device an order of the trained neural network module cascaded after the pre-training model and a set of input signals from a set of Transmission Reception Points (TRPs) to be input to the terminal device, and perform Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) positioning by using the set of input signals from the set of TRPs in the order described above based on the trained neural network module cascaded after the pre-training model.

In a second aspect, a network device is provided. The network device may include at least one processor and at least one memory storing instructions that, when executed by the at least one processor, cause the network device to at least receive a request from a terminal device for a neural network module cascaded after a pre-training model, train the neural network module based on data from a set of Transmission Reception Points (TRPs) selected by the terminal device, and send to the terminal device a sequence of the trained neural network module cascaded after the pre-training model, and a set of input signals from the set of TRPs to be input to the pre-training model cascaded with the trained neural network module at the terminal device.

In a third aspect, a method is provided. The method may include transmitting a request to a network device for a neural network module cascaded after a pre-training model, receiving from the network device an order of the trained neural network module cascaded after the pre-training model and a set of input signals from a set of Transmission Reception Points (TRPs) to be input to a terminal device, and performing Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) positioning by using the set of input signals from the set of TRPs in the order based on the trained neural network module cascaded after the pre-training model.

In a fourth aspect, a method is provided. The method may include receiving a request from a terminal device for a neural network module cascaded after a pre-training model, training the neural network module based on data from a set of Transmission Reception Points (TRPs) selected by the terminal device, and transmitting to the terminal device a sequence of trained neural network modules cascaded after the pre-training model, and a set of input signals from the set of TRPs to be input to the pre-training model cascaded with the trained neural network module at the terminal device.

In a fifth aspect, an apparatus is provided. The apparatus may include means for sending a request to a network device for a neural network module cascaded after a pre-training model, means for receiving from the network device an order of the trained neural network module cascaded after the pre-training model and a set of input signals from a set of Transmission Reception Points (TRPs) to be input to a terminal device, and means for performing Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) positioning by using the set of input signals from the set of TRPs in the order based on the trained neural network module cascaded after the pre-training model.

In a sixth aspect, an apparatus is provided. The apparatus may include means for receiving a request from a terminal device for a neural network module to cascade after a pre-training model, means for training the neural network module based on data from a set of Transmission Reception Points (TRPs) selected by the terminal device, and means for transmitting to the terminal device a trained neural network module to cascade after the pre-training model, and a sequence of sets of input signals from the set of TRPs to be input to the pre-training model to cascade with the trained neural network module at the terminal device.

In a seventh aspect, there is provided a non-transitory computer readable medium comprising program instructions which, when executed by an apparatus, cause the apparatus to perform at least the method according to the third aspect.

In an eighth aspect, there is provided a non-transitory computer readable medium comprising program instructions which, when executed by an apparatus, cause the apparatus to perform at least the method according to the fourth aspect.

In a ninth aspect, there is provided a computer program comprising instructions that, when executed by an apparatus, cause the apparatus to at least send a request to a network device for a neural network module cascaded after a pre-training model, receive from the network device an order of the trained neural network module cascaded after the pre-training model and a set of input signals from a set of Transmission Reception Points (TRPs) to be input to a terminal device, and perform Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) positioning by using the set of input signals from the set of TRPs in the order described above based on the trained neural network module cascaded after the pre-training model.

In a tenth aspect, there is provided a computer program comprising instructions that, when executed by an apparatus, cause the apparatus to at least receive a request from a terminal device for a neural network module cascaded after a pre-training model, train the neural network module based on data from a set of Transmission Reception Points (TRPs) selected by the terminal device, and send to the terminal device an order of the trained neural network module cascaded after the pre-training model, and a set of input signals from the set of TRPs to be input to the pre-training model cascaded with the trained neural network module at the terminal device.

In an eleventh aspect, a terminal device is provided. The terminal device may include transmit circuitry configured to transmit a request to a network device for a neural network module cascaded after a pre-training model, receive circuitry configured to receive from the network device an order of the trained neural network module cascaded after the pre-training model and a set of input signals from a set of Transmission Reception Points (TRPs) to be input to the terminal device, and execute circuitry configured to perform Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) positioning by using the set of input signals from the set of TRPs in the order based on the trained neural network module cascaded after the pre-training model.

In a twelfth aspect, a network device is provided. The network device may include receive circuitry configured to receive a request from a terminal device for a neural network module to cascade after a pre-training model, training circuitry configured to train the neural network module based on data from a set of Transmission Reception Points (TRPs) selected by the terminal device, and transmit circuitry configured to transmit to the terminal device a sequence of trained neural network modules to cascade after the pre-training model, and a set of input signals from the set of TRPs to be input to the pre-training model to cascade with the trained neural network module at the terminal device.

It should be understood that the summary is not intended to identify key or essential features of the embodiments of the disclosure, nor is it intended to be used to limit the scope of the disclosure. Other features of the present disclosure will become apparent from the following description.

Detailed Description

With the development of communication technology, 3GPP release 18 has approved research to enhance the benefits of the air interface through recent advances in the AI/ML field, and AI/ML positioning accuracy enhancement is seen as one of three most representative use cases, (a) Channel State Information (CSI) feedback enhancement (e.g., overhead reduction, accuracy improvement, prediction), (b) beam management (e.g., beam prediction in the time and/or spatial domain to reduce overhead and delay, improve beam selection accuracy), and (c) improving positioning accuracy for different scenarios, including scenarios with severe NLOS conditions.

For direct AI/ML positioning, the Channel Impulse Response (CIR)/Power Delay Profile (PDP) has been agreed to be entered as a candidate model for AI/ML positioning. However, the impact of specifications on new model inputs needs to be further investigated for trade-offs between model performance, model complexity, and computational complexity.

In view of the above, some embodiments of the present disclosure propose a solution for improving AI/ML positioning, e.g., balancing positioning accuracy and model training and storage consumption. In some example embodiments of the present disclosure, the network device trains the NN module based on a pre-training model and according to a number and combination TRP selected by the terminal device for direct AI/ML positioning. Thus, the trained NN module is specific to the particular TRP mode (both number and combination) indicated by the terminal device, and the terminal device may perform AI/ML localization based on the downloaded or received trained NN module concatenated after the pre-training model. That is, for a particular TPR pattern indicated by the terminal device, the network device trains only one lightweight custom NN model, and even with a small number of selected TRPs for a particular TRP pattern, AI/ML positioning accuracy meets the accuracy requirements, thus achieving a tradeoff between model performance, model complexity, and computational complexity.

For purposes of illustration, principles and example embodiments of the present disclosure for an ML framework for enhanced positioning will be described below with reference to fig. 1-9. It should be noted, however, that these examples are given so that those skilled in the art will be able to understand the inventive concepts of the present disclosure and implement the solutions presented herein, and are not intended to limit the scope of the present disclosure in any way.

Fig. 1 illustrates an example network environment 100 in which example embodiments of the present disclosure may be implemented. The environment 100, which may be part of a communication network, includes terminal devices and network devices. As shown in fig. 1, the communication network 100 may include a terminal device 110 (hereinafter may also be referred to as a user equipment 110 or UE 110). The communication network 100 may also include a network device 120, a network device 130 (hereinafter also referred to as a transmitter/receiver point (TRP) or station), and a network device 140 (hereinafter also referred to as an access network device including a Location Management Function (LMF)). In DL positioning, the network devices or TRPs 120 and 130 may send Positioning Reference Signals (PRSs) to the terminal device 110 and the network device 140 may request the UE 110 to collect PRS samples for each selected TRP 120 or 130.

It should be understood that the number of network devices and terminal devices is for illustration purposes only and is not meant to be limiting in any way. Further, the communications may utilize any suitable wireless communication technology including, but not limited to, multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM), time Division Multiplexing (TDM), frequency Division Multiplexing (FDM), code Division Multiplexing (CDM), bluetooth, zigBee, and Machine Type Communications (MTC), enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB), large-scale machine type communications (mMTC), ultra-reliable low-delay communications (URLLC), carrier Aggregation (CA), dual Connectivity (DC), and new radio unlicensed (NR-U) technologies.

It should be understood that the number of devices and their connection relationships and types shown in fig. 1 are for illustrative purposes only and are not meant to be limiting in any way. Communication system 100 may include any suitable number of devices suitable for implementing embodiments of the present disclosure.

In the 3GPP RAN1#112 discussion, CIR/PDP has been agreed to be entered as a candidate model for AI/ML localization. The impact of specifications on new model inputs has been agreed to be studied for trade-offs between model performance, model complexity, and computational complexity. In the latest 3GPP RAN1#112-e conference, the performance, overhead, and complexity of evaluating model input sizes for different approaches have been agreed. To evaluate AI/ML based localization, the study of model inputs for different TRP numbers included the following methods. The supporters of each approach analyze model performance, signaling overhead (including training data collection and model reasoning), model complexity, and computational complexity.

For method 1, where the model input size remains constant at ntrp=18, the number of TRPs (N' TRPs) that provide measurements for the model input will vary. When N 'TRP < NTRP, the remaining (NTRP-N' TRP) TRPs do not provide a measurement to the model input, i.e., the measurement is set to 0. As for method 1-A, the set of TRPs providing the measurement (N' TRPs) is fixed. As for method 1-B, the set of TRPs (N' TRPs) providing the measurement may be dynamically varied. It should be noted that for method 1, a model is provided to cover the whole evaluation area.

For method 2, where the TRP size of the model input is equal to the number of TRPs (N ' TRP) that are provided as model inputs, the given model ignores the remaining (NTRP-N ' TRP) when N ' TRP < NTRP. The set of TRP (N' TRP) providing the measurement is fixed for a given AI/ML model. With respect to method 2-A, a model can be provided to cover the entire assessment area, which is equivalent to deploying N ' TRP's for localization in the assessment area, ignoring the potential inferences of the remaining (18-N ' TRP) TRPs. With respect to method 2-B, if Nmodel (Nmodel > 1) models are provided to cover the entire assessment area, the total complexity (model complexity is the sum of Nmodel models).

The inventors of the present disclosure have evaluated the two methods described above, namely method 1 and method 2. For method 1, in the evaluation, the model input parameter size was fixed to ntrp=18 for all cases. When a subset of 18 TRPs is considered, the remaining unselected TRPs are set to zero. The positioning accuracy and model complexity are shown in table 1 below. However, as shown in table 1, when the number of TRPs of the input CIR/PDP signal is small (e.g., 4 TRP, 8 TRP, 12 TRP), positioning accuracy is very poor.

Table 1 for method 1, considering any TRP selection, different numbers of TRP (N TRP) gaps are evaluated and compared with their corresponding model complexity and computational complexity. The input parameters are PDP, N' t=128, ue distribution area=120×60m.

As shown in table 1, when the number of TRPs of the input CIR/PDP signal is small (e.g., 4 TRP, 8 TRP, 12 TRP), positioning accuracy is quite low. For example, when 4 TRPs are used, the horizontal 2D error (measured in meters) at CDF 90% is about 57.7m, when 8 TRPs are used, the horizontal 2D error (measured in meters) at CDF 90% is about 32.84m, and when 12 TRPs are used, the horizontal 2D error (measured in meters) at CDF 90% is about 21.06m. It is clear that the positioning accuracy does not correspond to the required accuracy, such as about 1 meter.

For method 2, in the evaluation, the inventors have trained many specific models of specific TRP patterns with N TRPs. As shown in table 2, in the case where the number of TRP is small, the positioning accuracy is far higher than that of method 1. However, to accommodate different TRP patterns in real world implementations, training and storage should be performed() A model in which N is the number of TRPs in TRP mode would result in a huge waste of computing power and memory storage.

Table 2 for method 2, considering any TRP selection, a different number of TRPs (N TRP) are evaluated and compared with their corresponding model complexity and computational complexity. The input parameters are PDP, N' t=128, ue distribution area=120×60m.

As shown in table 2, when the number of TRPs of the input CIR/PDP signal is, for example, 4 TRP, 8 TRP, 12 TRP, the positioning accuracy is 2.3317m, 2.5684m, and 1.3404m, respectively. However, as described above, for each specific TRP pattern with N TRPs, it should be trained and stored() A model that would result in a significant waste of computing resources and memory storage.

Based on the above observations, referring to the above-described evaluation of method 1, when a generic TRP mode model is deployed at the UE, positioning accuracy may be very poor when only a small subset of TRPs are connected to the UE. With reference to the evaluation of method 2 above, acceptable positioning accuracy can be achieved when a particular TRP pattern model is deployed at the UE, which model is only applicable to particular TRP patterns (number and combination of TRPs), however, when the TRP patterns (number or combination of TRPs) are changed, a new particular TRP pattern model needs to be trained and stored, which consumes a lot of computing power and memory.

In order to balance positioning accuracy and resource consumption (computational power and memory storage, such as model training computational resources and storage consumption), some embodiments of the present disclosure propose a solution for improving Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Learning (ML) positioning, in particular a solution for deploying TRP-dependent lightweight NN modules for direct AI/ML positioning based on a pre-trained TRP-agnostic generic basic model (TAB model).

Hereinafter, an example signal process 200 for performing AI/ML positioning will be described with reference to fig. 2. For discussion purposes, the process 200 may be described with reference to fig. 1. Process 200 may involve terminal device 110 and network device 140 as shown in fig. 1. It should be appreciated that although the process 200 is described in the communication environment 100 of fig. 1, the process is equally applicable to other communication scenarios with similar problems.

As shown in fig. 2, in process 200, terminal device 110 sends (205) a request to network device 140 for a Neural Network (NN) module to cascade after a pre-training model. The network device 140 receives (210) the request. The network device 140 may be a Location Management Function (LMF). As for the pre-training model, details will be described below with reference to fig. 4. In some embodiments, the pre-trained model is a pre-trained TRP agnostic generic base model (TAB model) for direct AI/ML localization. The terminal device 110 maintains a pre-trained TAB model and the TAB model may be pre-trained by the network device 140 (e.g., LMF). Before sending the request, the terminal device 110 may query the network device 140 as to whether the same TAB model is also maintained. If the network device 140 maintains the TAB model, the network device 140 will send an acknowledgement message to the terminal device 110 and the terminal device 110 will then send the request to the network device 140.

As shown in fig. 2, in process 200, network device 140 trains (215) NN modules based on data from a set of Transmission Reception Points (TRPs) selected by terminal device 110. The set of TRPs (e.g., TRPs 120 and 130) is selected by terminal device 110, and terminal device 110 may send an index of the selected TRPs to network device 140, and network device 140 may then train the NN module using data from the selected TRPs. In some embodiments, the trained NN module is a lightweight custom NN module that is cascaded after the TAB model. Training of the NN module will be described in detail below with reference to fig. 5.

As shown in fig. 2, in process 200, the network device 140 transmits (220) a sequence of trained NN modules concatenated after the pre-training model and a set of input signals from the set of TRPs to be input to the terminal device 110. The terminal device 110 receives (225) the trained NN module and the order. When entered into a pre-trained model (such as a TAB model) maintained at the terminal device 110, the input signal set from the selected TRP set should follow this order. The order of the input signal sets to be input to the terminal device 110 may be the same as the order of the data from the TRP sets to be used by the network device 140 for training the NN module. That is, when the NN module is trained at the network device 140, data from the TRP sets are input into the model in a particular order, and when the input signal sets are to be input into the terminal device 110, they may be input in that particular order.

As shown in fig. 2, in process 200, the terminal device 110 performs (230) Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) localization by using input signal sets from TRP sets in the order described above based on trained NN modules cascaded after a pre-training model. In some embodiments, the input signals from the set of TRPs may include a Channel Impulse Response (CIR) signal or a Power Delay Profile (PDP) signal, and each input signal may have an index of the corresponding TRP.

In the process 200 of the present disclosure, based on a pre-training model (such as a TAB model), the network device 140 trains the lightweight NN module according to the number and combined TRP selected by the terminal device 110 for direct AI/ML localization. That is, the trained NN module is specific to a particular TRP pattern (number and combination of TRPs) indicated by the terminal device 110. The terminal device 100 then downloads and deploys the trained NN module at the output of the pre-training model, that is, the downloaded trained NN module cascades after the pre-training model. The terminal device 100 may then perform AI/ML localization based on the trained NN modules cascaded after the pre-training model. That is, for a particular TPR pattern with N selected TRPs indicated by the terminal device, the network device only trains and stores one lightweight custom NN model for that particular TPR pattern, rather than according to method 2 aboveAnd therefore, the training complexity, the computing power and the storage memory are remarkably reduced. Furthermore, for each TRP mode, when direct AI/ML localization is performed, the trained NN module is concatenated after the pre-trained generic model, both the trained NN module and the trained generic model will contribute to the calculation of the localization coordinates, and thus the AI/ML localization accuracy will meet the accuracy requirement and will be higher than the accuracy obtained by method 1 above, even if a specific TRP mode has several selected TRPs.

Hereinafter, an example signaling procedure for deploying a custom Neural Network (NN) module cascaded after freezing a TAB model at a terminal device side for direct AI/ML localization according to some embodiments of the present disclosure will be described with reference to fig. 3.

As shown in fig. 3, at step 0, the UE 110 should maintain the TAB model, which is a prerequisite for the framework. For example, the network device (e.g., LMF 140) may pre-train the TAB model. At step 1, the UE 110 queries, e.g., via a message, whether the LMF 140 maintains the same TAB model. If the LMF 140 does not maintain the same TAB model, the process will terminate.

If the LMF 140 maintains the same TAB model, the process will continue. At step 2, LMF 140 will send an acknowledgement to UE 110 via the new message to maintain the same TAB model. When receiving an acknowledgement from the LMF 140 to maintain the same TAB model, the UE 110 sends a request for a lightweight custom NN module cascaded after the TAB model to the LMF 140 for direct AI/ML positioning via a new message at step 3. As shown in fig. 3, at step 4, UE 110 indicates to LMF 140 the index of TRPs 120 and 130 that it selects. For example, the index of the selected TRP is #9#15#18.

At step 5, the LMF 140 trains TRP-related lightweight Neural Network (NN) modules cascaded after the TAB model using data from the selected subset of TRPs (e.g., TRPs 120 and 130) for direct AI/ML localization. It should be noted that during the training process, the TAB model is frozen and the parameters of the TAB model are not tuned, only the parameters in the lightweight custom NN module are tuned. The CIR/PDP signals from the selected subset of TRPs are fed into the TAB model in a configured TRP index order. For example, the configured TRP index order is #15#18#9, rather than the index of the selected TRP indicated by UE 110 (e.g., #9#15# 18).

At step 6, LMF 140 sends the trained TRP-related lightweight NN module to UE 110. As shown in fig. 3, at step 7, LMF 140 indicates to UE 110 the TRP index order of the input signal (e.g., # 15#18#9) for use by UE 110 in feeding the signal into a TRP-related lightweight NN module cascaded after the TAB model at UE 110 for direct AI/ML positioning. For example, if the index of the selected TRP is #9#15#18, then the TRP index order of the input signals is configured by LMF 140 to #15#18#9, then these signals should be input into the model by UE 110 in order #15#18#9 (instead of #9#15#18 or other index order).

At step 8, LMF 140 indicates the selected TRP index (e.g., # 9#15#18) to the selected TRP. As shown in fig. 3, at step 9, the selected TRP transmits the CIR/PDP signal and its TRP index to UE 110. At step 10, AI/ML positioning is performed by UE 110 with the received CIR/PDP signal from the selected TRP in the indicated input order (e.g., order # 15#18#9) using the TAB model of the cascaded TRP-related lightweight NN module. It should be noted that the number of TRPs 120 and 130 is not limited to two TRPs, and TRPs 120 and 130 are illustrated for illustrative purposes only.

Thus, in some embodiments of the present disclosure, a solution is presented for deploying TRP-related lightweight NN modules on the UE side based on a pre-trained TRP-agnostic generic base model (TAB model) for direct AI/ML localization. In this solution, the NW (e.g., LMF 140) pre-trains the TAB model in advance and then trains the TRP-related lightweight NN module according to the UE's request in a dynamic TRP-oriented scenario. The UE 110 also maintains the same pre-trained TAB model as a prerequisite and then requests and downloads a TAB compatible lightweight custom NN module from the LMF 140, which can cascade immediately after the TAB model. Since the TAB model is a generic TRP agnostic pre-training model, when UE 110 receives CIR/PDP signals from any TRP pattern (the number of TRPs is denoted as M), these signals will pass through the TAB model to generate M intermediate outputs. The M intermediate outputs are then fed to cascaded custom NN modules to generate positioning results, such as two-dimensional positioning coordinates. Here, cascaded custom NN modules learn TRP-related localization by merging M intermediate features from a particular TRP pattern.

In a second scenario, the evaluation is based on baseline ViT, baseline ViT being a particular TRP pattern model trained according to conventional method 2 described above, with 196646 data samples for training and the remaining data samples for testing.

Hereinafter, an example implementation for training a generic model (such as a TAB model) according to some embodiments of the present disclosure will be described with reference to fig. 4.

As shown in fig. 4, the TAB model is an image text cross-modality pre-training model, which consists of two key feature extractors/encoders. A first key feature extractor or encoder is associated with an environment semantic embedding block < text encoder > that a description of the physical environment (e.g., NLOS/NLOS classification, BS (TRP) location, UE location, environment classification, etc.) is entered in the form of natural language text. A second key feature extractor or encoder is associated with the wireless channel feature extraction block < image encoder > that wireless channel features (e.g., CSI, CIR, PDP, etc.) are input in the form of images.

By maximizing the similarity between output matrices from different models, the text encoder and the image encoder are jointly trained to align multimodal information in a shared embedding space, thereby enabling cross-modal semantic understanding and matching. Thus, the text image learns the inherent wireless environment knowledge across the modal basis model and becomes a common model with unknown TRP patterns.

It should be noted that text encoding will be used when training the TAB model, and not when training the lightweight NN module and when performing AI/ML positioning. That is, in training the lightweight NN module, data from the selected TRP may be input into the image encoder of the TAB model to generate a corresponding intermediate output, and the intermediate output may be input into the NN module to generate 2D positioning coordinates. Therefore, the text encoder is not used in training the NN module. In performing AI/ML localization, a similar process will be performed and a text encoder will not be used.

Hereinafter, an example implementation for training a lightweight custom Neural Network (NN) module cascaded after freezing a TAB model according to some embodiments of the present disclosure will be described with reference to fig. 5.

The pre-trained TAB model provides a powerful initial starting point since it learns useful representations and semantic relationships between images and text during the pre-training phase. Thus, based on the ability to inherit and build pre-trained TAB models, a lightweight custom NN module is trained to align with the direct AI/ML localization task.

As shown in fig. 5, the lightweight custom NN module is cascaded after the image encoder of the TAB model. While training the cascaded NN module, the image encoder is frozen so that the parameters of the image encoder of the pre-trained TAB model will not be tuned and only the parameters of the lightweight custom NN module will be tuned. Training lightweight custom NN modules using data from selected TRPs, such as TRP #1#2#3, in a specific input order, such as TRP # 2#3#1. This means that the input to the image encoder is a sample set comprising a plurality of CSI samples from the selected TRP in a specific order (e.g. trp#2#3#1). By inputting CSI sample groups with a specific input order into the image encoder, output vectors from the same sample groups are concatenated in the same specific order and used as one input to a lightweight custom NN module to obtain corresponding positioning coordinates.
